links.reason: Luke has a voice from heaven say “You are My beloved Son”; Genesis has God say “your only son Isaac, whom you love.”
Luke says a man is to “raise up offspring for him”; Genesis has Judah tell Onan to “raise up offspring for your brother.”
Luke says Moses calls the Lord “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac”; in Exodus, God says “I am the God of your father.”
Luke says Moses calls the Lord “the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”; in Exodus, God says, “This is My name forever.”
Luke says “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”; Exodus has God say “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male.”
Luke says “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”; Exodus says to “present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb.”
Luke says “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated”; Exodus says the LORD killed Egypt’s firstborn, so “I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male.”
Luke lists “honor your father and mother” among the commandments; Exodus has the same words, then a promise of long days.
Luke lists “do not murder” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not murder.”
Luke lists “Do not commit adultery” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Luke lists “do not steal” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Luke lists “do not bear false witness” among the commandments; Exodus adds “against your neighbor.”
Luke says “I will send My messenger ahead of You”; Exodus says “I am sending an angel before you.”
Luke repeats “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”; Leviticus names “two turtledoves or two young pigeons” for one who cannot afford a lamb.
Luke repeats “Love your neighbor as yourself” after the command to love the Lord your God; Leviticus has the same words.
Luke lists “honor your father and mother” among the commandments; Deuteronomy has “Honor your father and your mother.”
Luke lists “do not murder” among the commandments; Deuteronomy says “You shall not murder.”
Luke gives the command “Do not commit adultery”; Deuteronomy says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Luke lists “do not steal” among the commandments; Deuteronomy says “You shall not steal.”
Luke lists “do not bear false witness” among the commandments; Deuteronomy gives “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.”
Luke repeats Deuteronomy’s command to love the LORD your God “with all your heart and with all your soul” and “with all your strength.”
Luke has Jesus answer with “Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only”; Deuteronomy says “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only.”
Luke has Jesus answer, “Do not put the Lord your God to the test”; Deuteronomy says, “Do not test the LORD your God.”
Luke has Jesus say “Man shall not live on bread alone”; Deuteronomy says man “does not live on bread alone.”
Luke has a voice from the cloud say, “Listen to Him!”; Deuteronomy says the LORD will raise up a prophet: “You must listen to him.”
Luke says Moses wrote that the man “is to marry his brother’s widow”; Deuteronomy says “Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife.”
Luke says God “has looked with favor on” His servant; 1 Samuel has a vow: “look upon the affliction of Your maidservant.”
Luke says of Jesus what 1 Samuel says of the boy Samuel: he grew “in stature and in favor with” God and man.
Luke has James and John ask to “call down fire from heaven”; Elijah in 2 Kings says “fire come down from heaven.”
Luke has James and John ask to “call down fire from heaven”; Elijah in 2 Kings says “fire come down from heaven.”
Luke has a voice from heaven say “You are My beloved Son”; Psalms says “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
Luke has a voice from the cloud say “This is My Son, whom I have chosen”; Psalms says “You are My Son.”
Luke has “Depart from me, all you evildoers”; Psalms has “Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.”
Luke says they “divided up His garments by casting lots”; Psalms says “They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.”
Luke has Jesus say “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit”; Psalms 31:5 says “Into Your hands I commit my spirit.”
Luke repeats “He will command His angels concerning You to guard You”; Psalms 91:11 continues “in all your ways.”
Luke repeats Psalms, which says, “They will lift you up in their hands,” so that the foot does not strike a stone.
Luke repeats Psalms: mercy “extends to those who fear Him”; Psalms speaks of the loving devotion of the LORD.
Luke says David himself speaks in the book of Psalms: “Sit at My right hand”.
Luke repeats Psalms: “until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”.
Luke has the Son of Man “seated at the right hand of the power of God”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Luke repeats Psalms: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone”.
Luke repeats Psalms: “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord”.
Luke repeats “who comes in the name of the Lord” from Psalms, and adds “the King” after “Blessed is”.
Luke has a man who “planted a vineyard”; Isaiah has a song: “My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill”.
Luke says “though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand”; Isaiah says “ever seeing, but never perceiving”.
Luke repeats “in darkness” and “the shadow of death” from Isaiah, where Isaiah says “a light has dawned”.
Luke asks “will you be lifted up to heaven?”; Isaiah says “I will ascend to the heavens”.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “you will be brought down to” Hades, where Isaiah has Sheol.
Luke says it will come upon “all who dwell on the face of all the earth”; Isaiah says terror awaits “O dweller of the earth”.
Luke says “The blind receive sight” and “the deaf hear”; Isaiah says “the eyes of the blind will be opened”.
Luke says “the lame walk”; Isaiah says “the lame will leap like a deer”.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “A voice of one calling” and “Prepare the way for the Lord”; Luke places “in the wilderness” after the voice.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “every mountain and hill made low”; Luke says the valley is “filled in” where Isaiah says “lifted up”.
Luke has “all humanity will see God’s salvation”; Isaiah has “all humanity together will see it”.
Luke has a voice from heaven say “in You I am well pleased”; Isaiah says “My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights”.
Luke has a voice from the cloud say “This is My Son, whom I have chosen”; Isaiah says “My Chosen One”.
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words “He was numbered with the transgressors” as something that must happen “in Me.”
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words about “a house of prayer,” but leaves out “called” and “for all the nations.”
Luke says “to release the oppressed”; Isaiah’s fast is “to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke.”
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words “to preach good news to the poor” and “to proclaim liberty to the captives.”
Luke gives a reply that ends “the good news is preached to the poor”; Isaiah says “to preach good news to the poor.”
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words about proclaiming “the year of the” Lord’s favor; Isaiah then adds “the day of our God’s vengeance.”
Luke repeats Jeremiah’s words “a den of robbers,” said of a house that Jeremiah says “bears My Name.”
Luke says “your house is left to you desolate”; Jeremiah says “this house will become a pile of rubble” if the words are not obeyed.
Luke repeats Daniel’s picture of “the Son of Man coming” in a cloud, where Daniel has “the clouds of heaven.”
Luke repeats Hosea’s words “they will say to the mountains” and “to the hills,” but swaps the two cries, “Fall on us!” and “Cover us!”
Luke says family members “will be divided,” including mother against daughter; Micah says “a daughter rises against her mother.”
Luke says the child will go before the Lord to “prepare the way for Him”; Malachi has “who will prepare the way before Me.”
Luke repeats Malachi’s words “Behold, I will send My messenger” and “who will prepare,” changing “before Me” to “before You.”
Luke says the crowds asked, “What then should we do?”; Malachi says “you ask,” and the people say, “How can we return?”
Luke says he will go before the Lord “in the spirit and power of Elijah”; Malachi says “I will send you Elijah the prophet.”
Luke repeats Malachi’s words “turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.”
Luke repeats “with all your heart and with all your soul”; Deuteronomy 10:12 asks Israel to love and serve the LORD that way.
Luke repeats “with all your heart and with all your soul”; Deuteronomy says “you will love Him” that way, “so that you may live.”
